Title: A feasibility randomised controlled trial of targeted oxygen therapy in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients
Author: Martin et al.
Comment: Table 6 reports survivors, not deaths, and one participant per arm had missing 90-day status. Known deaths were obtained as randomized total minus reported alive minus reported missing: conservative 17−9−1=7; higher/usual-care 17−11−1=5. In accordance with the synthesis contract, denominators retain all 17 randomized participants per arm. No treatment-comparison test or RR was reported by the paper.
Study Environment: Two intensive care units in NHS hospitals in England
Topic of Content: Conservative versus usual-care oxygenation in mechanically ventilated critically ill adults
Participant type: Mechanically ventilated adults aged 18 years or older with acute respiratory failure admitted to ICU
Recruitment source: Royal Free Hospital, London, and Southampton General Hospital intensive care units
Outcome measurement: Death from any cause by 90 days, derived from Table 6 vital status while retaining all randomized participants as denominators
effect_direction: Lower mortality with higher/liberal oxygen (5/17) than with lower/conservative oxygen (7/17); RR should be oriented higher versus lower.

Title: Low versus high pulse oxygen saturation directed oxygen therapy in critically ill patients: a randomized controlled pilot study
Author: Yang, Shang, and Yuan
Comment: The paper did not directly report an RR or confidence interval, so those fields are left null. For synthesis, orient the derived comparison as high/liberal oxygen divided by low/conservative oxygen; the paper lists the low-target arm first.
Design Type: Prospective single-center parallel-group randomized controlled pilot trial
Study Environment: General intensive care unit, single center
Topic of Content: Higher versus lower pulse oxygen saturation targets
Recruitment source: Patients admitted to the ICU with an expected ICU stay of 72 hours or longer
Outcome measurement: Death from any cause within 28 days after inclusion; weekly follow-up phone calls after discharge through day 28
effect_direction: Higher mortality with higher oxygen (37/114) than with lower oxygen (26/100); RR should be oriented higher versus lower.

Report_ID: Death from any cause at day 180
Title: Conservative Oxygen Therapy during Mechanical Ventilation in the ICU
Author: The ICU-ROX Investigators and the Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society Clinical Trials Group
Comment: For synthesis, randomized intention-to-treat denominators were used as instructed: 484 conservative and 481 usual. The paper's day-180 mortality percentages and reported effect estimates used available mortality data for 476 conservative and 475 usual participants. The reported odds ratio and hazard ratio are in the paper's conservative-versus-usual direction, whereas the planned pooled RR is to be calculated as usual/higher divided by conservative/lower from the extracted arm-level events and randomized totals.
Medium: Invasive mechanical ventilation in the ICU
Content length: Oxygen strategy applied until ICU discharge or day 28, whichever occurred earlier; mortality follow-up at day 180
Participant type: Adults (≥18 years) expected to receive mechanical ventilation in the ICU beyond the day after recruitment
Recruitment source: 21 ICUs in Australia and New Zealand
Outcome measurement: Death from any cause by day 180 after randomization
Outcome variable: Death from any cause at day 180
effect_direction: Slightly lower mortality with usual/higher oxygen (164/481) than with conservative/lower oxygen (170/484); RR should be oriented higher versus lower.

Report_ID: Death from any cause at day 90
Title: Liberal or Conservative Oxygen Therapy for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
Author: Barrot et al.
Comment: The paper reports 205 randomized participants but excludes four after randomization and provides day-90 mortality only for the analyzed groups (99 conservative and 102 liberal). Arm allocation and mortality outcomes for the four excluded participants are not stated, so the directly reported denominators were retained. The paper's adjusted hazard ratio is oriented for the conservative-versus-liberal survival comparison and was not entered as the planned synthesis uses arm-level risks oriented higher/liberal versus lower/conservative.
Design Type: Prospective multicenter randomized open-label parallel-group controlled trial
domain: Critical care oxygen therapy for acute respiratory distress syndrome
Medium: Invasive mechanical ventilation in the ICU
Content length: Oxygen targets applied for 7 days or until earlier extubation; mortality assessed at day 90
Topic of Content: Liberal versus conservative arterial oxygenation targets
interaction_type: Clinician-managed oxygen therapy according to randomized PaO2 and SpO2 targets
Participant type: Adults with ARDS who were intubated and mechanically ventilated
Outcome measurement: Death from any cause by 90 days after randomization
Outcome variable: Death from any cause at day 90
effect_direction: Lower mortality with liberal/higher oxygen (31/102) than with conservative/lower oxygen (44/99); RR should be oriented higher versus lower.

Report_ID: Death from any cause within 90 days after randomization
Title: Lower or Higher Oxygenation Targets for Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure
Author: Schjørring et al.
Comment: Per the synthesis contract, event denominators use all randomized participants (1462 lower oxygen; 1466 higher oxygen), although the paper reports the primary mortality analysis as 618/1441 and 613/1447 because mortality data were unavailable or unusable for some randomized participants. The paper's adjusted RR of 1.02 (0.94 to 1.11) is oriented as lower oxygenation versus higher oxygenation, opposite the planned meta-analysis orientation of higher versus lower; use the arm-level events and randomized totals to calculate the synthesis RR rather than treating the reported RR as higher-versus-lower.
Design Type: Multicenter, stratified, parallel-group randomized clinical trial
Country: Denmark, Switzerland, Finland, the Netherlands, Norway, the United Kingdom, and Iceland
Medium: Supplemental oxygen therapy in the intensive care unit
Content length: Maximum intervention and follow-up period of 90 days
Topic of Content: Lower versus higher arterial oxygenation targets in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure
interaction_type: Clinician-managed oxygen therapy targeting assigned PaO2
Participant type: Adults aged at least 18 years admitted to the ICU with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure
Recruitment source: Patients enrolled at 35 ICUs in seven European countries
Outcome measurement: Death from any cause within 90 days after randomization, obtained from patient files and regional and national registries
Outcome variable: Death from any cause within 90 days after randomization
effect_direction: Slightly lower mortality with higher oxygen (613/1466) than with lower oxygen (618/1462) using randomized denominators; RR should be oriented higher versus lower.

Report_ID: Death from any cause at 90 days
Title: Oxygen Targets in Comatose Survivors of Cardiac Arrest
Author: Schmidt et al.
Comment: Table 2 lists restrictive oxygen first, so group 1 is the lower-oxygen control and group 2 is the higher-oxygen intervention. The reported hazard ratio of 0.93 (95% CI, 0.72–1.20) is explicitly defined by the table footnote and is oriented restrictive versus liberal; it must not be treated as the planned liberal-versus-restrictive risk ratio. For the planned synthesis, use the raw intention-to-treat counts: liberal 123/395 versus restrictive 113/394. Two participants were lost to follow-up and censored, but full randomized denominators are retained per the synthesis contract.
Design Type: Open-label randomized controlled trial with a 2-by-2 factorial design
Study Environment: Two tertiary cardiac arrest centers; intensive care unit
Medium: Supplemental oxygen administered during mechanical ventilation
Participant type: Comatose adults resuscitated after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
Recruitment source: Two tertiary cardiac arrest centers in Denmark
Outcome measurement: Death from any cause within 90 days after randomization
Outcome variable: Death from any cause at 90 days
effect_direction: Higher mortality with liberal/higher oxygen (123/395) than with restrictive/lower oxygen (113/394); RR should be oriented higher versus lower.

Title: Conservative versus liberal oxygenation targets for mechanically ventilated patients – a pilot multicenter randomized controlled trial
Author: Panwar et al.
Comment: The paper's Table 2 analyzed 52 conservative-arm participants after excluding one participant who withdrew consent, and its reported 40% corresponds to 21/52. Per the synthesis contract, the conservative-arm event denominator is retained as all 53 participants randomized; the liberal arm is 19/51. Thus the event totals for meta-analysis are 19/51 (liberal) versus 21/53 (conservative), while group_2_n=52 and n_total=103 reflect the paper's final analyzed sample. The paper did not report a risk ratio, so no RR was entered. The adjusted hazard ratio was not entered because it was reported in the opposite orientation (conservative versus liberal) and the synthesis requires arm-level risks oriented liberal versus conservative.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Liberal oxygenation strategy (target SpO2 ≥96%)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Prospective multicenter randomized parallel-group pilot controlled trial
domain: Critical care oxygen therapy and all-cause mortality
Study Environment: Four university-affiliated multidisciplinary intensive care units
interaction_type: Clinician/nurse titration of FiO2 to randomized SpO2 target
Participant type: Adult ICU patients expected to require invasive mechanical ventilation for at least 24 hours
Outcome measurement: Death from any cause by day 90 after randomization
effect_direction: Lower mortality with liberal/higher oxygen (19/51) than with conservative/lower oxygen (21/53) using randomized denominators; RR should be oriented higher versus lower.

Report_ID: All-cause mortality 30 days after cardiac arrest
Title: Targeting two different levels of both arterial carbon dioxide and arterial oxygen after cardiac arrest and resuscitation: a randomised pilot trial
Author: Jakkula et al.
Comment: The trial randomised 123 patients but reports 120 included in analyses; Table 2 oxygen-arm denominators (61 and 59) were used as instructed by the supplied extraction contract/pre-identified effect. This is a factorial trial, and the reported oxygen groups are marginal groups collapsed across the other randomised factors. The paper does not report an RR, so no risk ratio was entered.
Design Type: Prospective multicentre randomised controlled pilot trial with a 2^3 factorial design
Study Environment: Intensive care units at multiple centres
Medium: Mechanically delivered oxygen adjusted to arterial oxygen target
Topic of Content: Normoxia versus moderate hyperoxia after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
Participant type: Adult unconscious mechanically ventilated patients resuscitated from witnessed out-of-hospital cardiac arrest of presumed cardiac origin
Outcome measurement: Vital status at 30 days after cardiac arrest (dead or alive)
Outcome variable: All-cause mortality 30 days after cardiac arrest
effect_direction: Higher mortality with moderate hyperoxia/higher oxygen (20/59) than with normoxia/lower oxygen (18/61); RR should be oriented higher versus lower.

Title: Hyperoxia and hypertonic saline in patients with septic shock (HYPERS2S): a two-by-two factorial, multicentre, randomised, clinical trial
Author: Asfar et al.
Comment: The paper reports a Cox-regression p value for this row but does not provide the day-90 hazard ratio in the supplied Results text/Table 2. No risk ratio was reported by the paper, so risk_ratio is left null; meta-analysis should calculate the RR from the extracted arm-level events and randomised/analysed intention-to-treat denominators. The oxygen-factor groups are pooled across the saline-factor assignments, as required for this factorial trial.
Design Type: Two-by-two factorial, multicentre, randomised clinical trial
domain: Critical care; septic shock; oxygen therapy
Study Environment: Intensive care units in 22 hospitals and academic centres
Content length: FiO2 1.0 for the first 24 h after inclusion in the hyperoxia arm
Topic of Content: Higher versus lower oxygen exposure in mechanically ventilated septic shock
Participant type: Adults aged 18 years or older with septic shock receiving mechanical ventilation
Recruitment source: 22 hospitals and academic centres in France
Outcome measurement: Death from any cause by day 90 after randomisation
effect_direction: Higher mortality with hyperoxia/higher oxygen (104/217) than with normoxia/lower oxygen (90/217); RR should be oriented higher versus lower.
